summary: Ravi M. Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Boise State University and the University of Oxford under mentors including Kenneth R. Valpey. He held posts at William & Mary and Utah State University, where he directed Religious Studies.

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Lucknow, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University. He served in the Haryana archaeology department and was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (c. 1983–2004).

Rawi Bhavilai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Chulalongkorn University, the University of Adelaide, and Australian National University. He was a physics professor (1945–1986) and director at Chulalongkorn University, and a fellow of the Royal Institute of Thailand.

Raymond West was an Indologist who studied under Martin Haug. He served as a Bombay High Court judge (1873–1887), Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (c. 1878–1886), Asiatic Society president, and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Cambridge (c. 1892–1900).
Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He succeeded Baker and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from around 1986 to 1995.

Rebecca Hufen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she studied at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk and served there as a lector for Tibetan Studies.

Rebecca Redwood French is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Washington and Yale University. She held law faculty posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 1996–2003) and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).
Rebecca Sundén is an Indology and Tibetology scholar attested in 2026 as studying and working as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg.

Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Mircea Eliade, Chögyam Trungpa, and others. He taught at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002) and served as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).
Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University and later served there as a professor (attested 1996).
Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya. He served as a teacher at Komazawa University (attested 1956).

Reiko Ohnuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at UC Berkeley and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. She held posts at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College (attested 2012).

Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He directed the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, served as president of Kyoto Women's University, and became professor emeritus at Tokyo and Ryukoku universities.

Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Ordentlicher Professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and as professor of philosophy at Heidelberg University from 1977.
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983–1984) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who completed his habilitation at the University of Leipzig (1826–1831). He served on Leipzig's faculty from 1832, becoming an außerordentlicher Professor in 1849 until his death in 1870.

Reinhold Niebuhr was a religious studies and philosophy scholar educated at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School. He served on the faculty at Union Theological Seminary from around 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena under Johann Gustav Stickel and Johann Gildemeister. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and Head Librarian at the India Office (1869–1893).
Reirin Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as president of Komazawa Junior College.
Remeen Firoz is an Indologist who is attested in 2026 as a PhD student at the Australian National University studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron.
